drg.description: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. 57-year-old female admitted for urinary tract infection. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.52, creatinine 0.94, hemoglobin 13.1, platelets 201, sodium 134, wbc 6.1; vitals dbp 64-69, heart_rate 77-81, map 82-86, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 15-16, sbp 119-126, spo2 96-97, temp 36.5-36.8
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Urinalysis: positive nitrites, >50 WBC/hpf; Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Type 2 diabetes.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 0.93, hemoglobin 13.1, platelets 205, sodium 139, wbc 5.9; vitals dbp 65-69, heart_rate 78-81, map 85-88, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 15-16, sbp 120-127, spo2 96-97, temp 36.6-36.8
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Type 2 diabetes. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 57-year-old female, length of stay 3 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Urinary tract infection. Type 2 diabetes. Follow up with primary care in one week. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed.
